android.alerts_collapse.note: Screen-reader name of the arrow at the right of a row of the Alerts tab that groups the device's errors, while its list of errors is shown: hides it.

android.alerts_expand.note: Screen-reader name of the arrow at the right of a row of the Alerts tab that groups the device's errors, while its list of errors is hidden: shows it.

android.alerts_friends.note: At the right of a friend request in the Alerts tab once you accepted it from there: you are friends now. Keep the check mark.

android.ble_lost.note: Set up a new device (over Bluetooth): error given to the setup page when the Bluetooth link dropped while a request was sent; the app reconnects.

android.ble_send_failed.text: Could not send to the device
android.ble_send_failed.note: Set up a new device (over Bluetooth): error given to the setup page when a request couldn't be written over Bluetooth.

android.bluetooth_needed_hint.text: Allow nearby devices for Off The Cloud in Settings to set a device up this way.
android.bluetooth_needed_hint.note: Set up a new device (over Bluetooth): under the heading Bluetooth access is needed. "Nearby devices" is Android's name for the Bluetooth permission and Settings the phone's Settings app: use Android's own words in this language.

android.bluetooth_off_hint.text: Turn Bluetooth on to find the device.
android.bluetooth_off_hint.note: Set up a new device (over Bluetooth): under the heading Bluetooth is off.

android.bluetooth_scan_failed.text: Couldn't start looking for devices. Turn Bluetooth off and on again.
android.bluetooth_scan_failed.note: Set up a new device (over Bluetooth): heading when the phone refused to look for devices over Bluetooth (a failed scan). Try again (common.try_again) follows.

android.bluetooth_turn_on.note: Button in Set up a new device (over Bluetooth) under the heading Bluetooth is off: asks the phone to turn Bluetooth on.

android.cache_bytes.note: Settings > Thumbnail cache: a size below one kilobyte (Using 0 bytes of 1 GB for an empty cache); larger sizes use the units KB, MB, GB.

android.compose_move_left.note: Screen-reader name of the left arrow under a picked photo in the New Post composer's strip of picked photos: moves it one place earlier in the post.

android.compose_move_right.note: Screen-reader name of the right arrow under a picked photo in the New Post composer's strip of picked photos: moves it one place later in the post.

android.compose_record_video.note: Item of the menu of the camera button in the New Post composer: opens the camera to record a video for the post.

android.compose_take_photo.note: Item of the menu of the camera button in the New Post composer: opens the camera to take a photo for the post.

android.download_changed.text: the file changed on the device while downloading
android.download_changed.note: Why opening or downloading a file failed, after Download failed: or similar (hence the lowercase start): the file was replaced on the device while it was being fetched.

android.download_empty_piece.text: the device sent an empty piece of the file
android.download_empty_piece.note: Why opening or downloading a file failed, after Download failed: or similar (hence the lowercase start): the device sent a piece without data before the end of the file.

android.download_wrong_piece.text: the device sent the wrong piece of the file
android.download_wrong_piece.note: Why opening or downloading a file failed, after Download failed: or similar (hence the lowercase start): a piece the device sent doesn't match the place asked for.

android.files.allow_deletions.note: Confirm button of the question app.files.allow_deletions_title (Files, a tap on an upload-only folder's lock): lets the folder's files be deleted again.

android.files.folder_update_failed_detai.note: Short message (toast) at the top of Files when making a folder upload only (or allowing deletions again), keeping it out of Images or showing it there again failed on the way. {detail} is the reason, from the app or the phone (it may be in the phone's own language).

android.files.gallery_clip_label.note: Label the phone may show for what Copy Link (app.files.gallery_copy_link) put on the clipboard: the gallery's link.

android.files.gallery_copy_failed.note: Error in the Share as Gallery dialog when the device stopped copying the photos and videos with an error and gave no reason (when it gives one, its own words are shown instead).

android.files.gallery_empty.text: There are no photos or videos here.
android.files.gallery_empty.note: Error in the Share as Gallery dialog when the folder or collection has nothing that can be shared.

text.one: There are no photos or videos here ({count} other file).
text.other: There are no photos or videos here ({count} other files).

android.files.gallery_empty_skipped.note: Error in the Share as Gallery dialog when the folder has no photos or videos, only other files, which galleries can't hold. {count} is how many other files there are.

android.files.gallery_expires.note: Heading of the choices of how long the gallery's link works (1, 7 or 30 days) in the Share as Gallery dialog.

android.files.gallery_failed_title.note: Title of the Share as Gallery dialog when making the gallery failed; the reason is under it. Title Case in English.

android.files.gallery_keep_open.text: Keep this open: the link is shown when the copy finishes.
android.files.gallery_keep_open.note: Under the progress bar of the Share as Gallery dialog while the device copies the photos and videos.

android.files.gallery_link_copied.note: Shown under the gallery's link in the Share as Gallery dialog once Copy Link was tapped.

android.files.gallery_link_once.text: This link is shown only now - the device never stores it. Share it or copy it before closing.
android.files.gallery_link_once.note: Text over the gallery's link in the Share as Gallery dialog once the gallery is ready.

android.files.gallery_looking.text: Looking at what will be shared…
android.files.gallery_looking.note: Shown with a spinner when the Share as Gallery dialog opens, while the device counts what will be shared.

android.files.gallery_lost.note: Error in the Share as Gallery dialog when the app couldn't ask the device how the copy was going five times in a row.

android.files.gallery_ready.note: Title of the Share as Gallery dialog once the gallery is made and its link is shown. Title Case in English.

android.files.gallery_skipped.note: Second line of the Share as Gallery dialog, before sharing, when the folder holds files that aren't photos or videos: they won't be in the gallery. {count} is how many.

android.files.inside_kept_out.text: Inside {folder}, which is kept out of Images
android.files.inside_kept_out.note: Says that the folder shown in Files is inside another folder that is kept out of Images. {folder} is that other folder (a path such as /Photos/Private). Images is the photo section (app.shell.section_images).

android.files.inside_kept_out_banner.text: Inside {folder}, which is kept out of Images - photos and videos here aren't tagged, searched for faces or shown in Images.
android.files.inside_kept_out_banner.note: Banner at the top of Files over a folder inside another folder kept out of Images, with a button to show that one in Images under it. {folder} is that other folder (a path such as /Photos/Private). Images is the photo section (app.shell.section_images).

android.files.inside_kept_out_info.text: Inside {folder}, which is kept out of Images. Photos and videos here aren't tagged, searched for faces or shown in Images. Files still shows them.
android.files.inside_kept_out_info.note: Explanation shown (title app.files.kept_out) when the mark of a folder is tapped in Files while the folder shown is inside another one kept out of Images. {folder} is that other folder (a path such as /Photos/Private). Images is the photo section (app.shell.section_images).

android.files.kept_out_said.note: Said by the screen reader (not shown) once a folder has been kept out of Images. {name} is the folder's name. Images is the photo section (app.shell.section_images).

android.files.show_named.note: Button of the banner at the top of Files (android.files.inside_kept_out_banner): asks whether to show the folder that keeps this one out of Images there again. {name} is that folder's name. Images is the photo section (app.shell.section_images). Write the quotes in your language's style.

android.files.shown_said.note: Said by the screen reader (not shown) once a folder kept out of Images is shown there again. {name} is the folder's name. Images is the photo section (app.shell.section_images).

android.files.wait_download_link.text: Wait for the download link to be ready
android.files.wait_download_link.note: Short message (toast) at the top of Files when keeping a folder out of Images (or showing it there) is asked while a download link for the selection is still being made. No full stop in English.

android.files.wait_folder.text: Wait for the folder to be updated
android.files.wait_folder.note: Short message (toast) at the top of Files when keeping a folder out of Images (or showing it there) is asked while another folder's change is still under way. No full stop in English.

android.files.wait_share_link.text: Wait for the share link to be ready
android.files.wait_share_link.note: Short message (toast) at the top of Files when keeping a folder out of Images (or showing it there) is asked while a share link for the selection is still being made. No full stop in English.

android.friends_ask_theirs_unnamed.text: Ask this friend's device to delete what I shared
android.friends_ask_theirs_unnamed.note: app.social.friends.ask_theirs for a friend with neither a profile name nor an address: a switch (off at first) when removing them that also asks their device to delete your posts, comments and likes there.

android.friends_delete_theirs.text: Delete everything from {name} on this phone
android.friends_delete_theirs.note: Check box (off at first) when removing a friend: also deletes everything of theirs from your device (explained by app.social.friends.delete_theirs_text). {name} is the friend's profile name (or their device's address when they have none).

android.friends_delete_theirs_unnamed.text: Delete everything from this friend on this phone
android.friends_delete_theirs_unnamed.note: android.friends_delete_theirs for a friend with neither a profile name nor an address: a check box (off at first) when removing them that also deletes everything of theirs from your device.

android.friends_keep.note: Button of the Remove (a friend)? dialog that closes it and keeps the friend.

android.friends_keep_waiting.note: Button of the confirmation app.social.friends.remove_now_title that closes it and keeps waiting for the friend's device.

android.friends_remove_friend.note: Button (in red) of the Remove (a friend)? dialog: removes the friend, deleting what its two check boxes say.

android.friends_remove_now.note: Button (in red) of the confirmation app.social.friends.remove_now_title: stops waiting for the friend's device and ends the friendship at once.

android.friends_remove_now_title_unnamed.note: app.social.friends.remove_now_title for a friend with neither a profile name nor an address: the confirmation asked before ending the friendship without waiting for their device.

android.friends_remove_title_unnamed.note: app.social.friends.remove_title for a friend with neither a profile name nor an address: the title of the dialog for removing them.

android.location_off_hint.text: Location is off. On this version of Android, the phone finds Bluetooth devices only with Location on.
android.location_off_hint.note: Set up a new device (over Bluetooth), on Android 11 and older: under the heading Looking for a device to set up… while the phone's Location is off, with Open Settings (android.open_settings) under it. Location is Android's setting of that name.

android.menu_sections.note: Screen-reader name of the left menu and of the icon rail (on a wide screen), not shown.

android.notification_channel.note: Name of the notification channel for pushes, shown in Android's notification settings for the app.

android.notification_channel_description.text: Friend requests, new posts, likes and comments
android.notification_channel_description.note: Description of that notification channel, shown under its name in Android's notification settings.

android.open_settings.note: Button in Set up a new device (over Bluetooth): opens the phone's Settings - at this app's page when it isn't allowed to use Bluetooth (android.bluetooth_needed_hint), at Location when that is off (android.location_off_hint). Settings is Android's own app: use its name in this language.

android.photos_open_in_maps.note: Button under the map in the panel with a photo's camera details: opens the place in the phone's maps app. {latitude} and {longitude} are the place's coordinates (40.41678, -3.70379).

android.photos_people_back.note: Screen-reader name of the back arrow at the start of the People page's bar: back to Images.

android.photos_people_deleting.note: On the Delete button of the confirmation (People page) while several people are being deleted, beside a spinner: which one is being deleted ({current}) of how many ({total}).

android.photos_people_keep.note: Screen-reader name of a face to choose in the merge's box (People page): choosing it keeps that person. {name} is their name (or app.shell.search_unnamed), {count} how many photos show them.

android.photos_people_merge_dimmed.note: Screen-reader name of the dimmed Merge item (app.photos.people.merge) of the bar shown while only one face is picked on the People page.

android.photos_search_close.note: Screen-reader name of the back arrow at the start of the search field that closes the search suggestions.

android.photos_search_in_search.note: Screen-reader name of the check mark beside a person in the search suggestions who is already a chip in the search.

android.settings.bridge_leave_delete.note: Button (in red) of the confirmation Delete your account?: the device leaves the bridge, then the account page opens to delete the account.

android.settings.crop_hint.text: Drag the photo to centre your face
android.settings.crop_hint.note: Above the square on the screen that crops the new profile photo to a circle.

android.settings.crop_zoom.note: Label of the zoom slider on the screen that crops the new profile photo.

android.settings.folder_on_volume.note: Second line of a folder on the Folders screen (Settings > Sync Options > Folders) when the folder is on a memory card or other storage rather than the phone's own: {volume} is that storage's name as Android gives it (SD card), {path} where the folder is on it (DCIM/Camera).

android.settings.folders.note: Row in Settings > Sync Options that opens the list of this phone's photo folders (Camera, Screenshots, WhatsApp Images...) with a switch for each, and that screen's title.

android.settings.folders_all.note: Value at the right of the Folders row in Settings > Sync Options when no folder is turned off: every folder is backed up. Agrees with folders.

android.settings.folders_empty.text: No photos on this phone yet.
android.settings.folders_empty.note: On the Folders screen (Settings > Sync Options > Folders) when the phone holds no photo at all.

android.settings.folders_footer.text: Turning a folder off only stops backing it up: nothing is deleted, from this phone or from your device. Turning it back on backs up everything already in it.
android.settings.folders_footer.note: Under the list on the Folders screen (Settings > Sync Options > Folders): what turning a folder's switch off, and on again, does. Your device is the Off The Cloud device.

android.settings.folders_hidden.text: Android hides folders whose name starts with a dot, and folders that contain a file called .nomedia, from every app, this one included. Their photos can't be listed here or backed up until the folder is renamed or that file is removed.
android.settings.folders_hidden.note: Last note on the Folders screen (Settings > Sync Options > Folders): why some folders aren't in the list. Keep .nomedia as it is: it is a file name.

android.settings.folders_intro.text: Every folder is backed up unless you turn it off here. New folders are backed up too, as soon as they appear.
android.settings.folders_intro.note: At the top of the Folders screen (Settings > Sync Options > Folders), above the list of the phone's photo folders and their switches.

android.settings.folders_load_failed.text: Could not list the folders on this phone.
android.settings.folders_load_failed.note: Error on the Folders screen (Settings > Sync Options > Folders) when Android didn't give the list of the phone's photos.

android.settings.folders_off.note: Value at the right of the Folders row in Settings > Sync Options: how many folders are turned off, so not backed up. Agrees with folders.

android.settings.free_up_footer.text: Photos and videos older than that are moved from this phone to its trash, each only once the device confirms it holds an exact copy. Android asks first, and the trash keeps them for 30 days. This happens after a sync while the app is open, at most once a day.
android.settings.free_up_footer.note: Under the Free Up Space section on Android (Settings, and the Sync Your Photos screen): what its switch does. "older than that": older than the time chosen just above (Older than 7 days). The trash is the phone's own (the system's), where deleted photos wait before they are gone.

android.settings.links_delete_text.text: The shared copies are deleted and the link stops working.
android.settings.links_delete_text.note: Message of the confirmation Delete this link? (app.settings.links.delete_title).

android.settings.links_empty_text.text: Links made with Share or Share as Gallery in Images and Files show up here until they expire.
android.settings.links_empty_text.note: Under No shared links on the Shared Links screen. Share and Share as Gallery are the names of buttons in Images and Files.

android.settings.logs_empty.note: Shown on the Logs screen when the chosen log is empty.

android.settings.logs_footer.text: What the device and its updates write down as they run - live, to read, share or send to us when something goes wrong.
android.settings.logs_footer.note: Under the Logs row in Settings: what the logs are.

android.settings.logs_load_failed.note: Error on the Logs screen when the log couldn't be read and the device gave no reason; the app tries again.

android.settings.logs_send_failed.note: Error after Send in the form that sends the logs, when they couldn't be sent and the device gave no reason.

android.settings.logs_send_title.note: Title of the form that sends the device's logs to Off The Cloud for help.

android.settings.picker_empty.note: Shown on the screen Choose a photo when the chosen collection (or the device) has no photo.

android.settings.picker_load_failed.note: Error on the screen Choose a photo when a page of photos couldn't be loaded; it is asked again.

android.settings.picker_open_failed.note: Error on the screen Choose a photo when the tapped photo couldn't be fetched or read.

android.settings.profile_description.note: Placeholder of the text field under the name in Settings > Profile: a few words about the user that friends see.

android.settings.profile_from_phone.note: Item of the Change photo menu in Settings > Profile: pick the profile photo among this phone's photos.

android.settings.sharing_footer.text: Galleries and download links you shared, until they expire. Deleting one removes the shared copies and the link stops working.
android.settings.sharing_footer.note: Under the Shared Links row in Settings > Sharing.

android.settings.sync_cloud.note: Switch in Settings > Sync Options: also upload photos kept only in the cloud (the phone downloads them first).

android.settings.sync_title.note: Heading of the section of Settings holding the Sync All and Sync From Now buttons.

android.settings.thumbs_change_size.note: What a screen reader says tapping does, on the Maximum size row of Settings > Thumbnail cache.

android.settings.thumbs_max_size_a11y.note: Screen-reader name of the Maximum size row of Settings > Thumbnail cache. {size} is the chosen size, already formatted (1 GB).

android.settings.thumbs_selected.note: Screen-reader name of the check mark next to the chosen size in the Maximum size menu of Settings > Thumbnail cache.

android.settings.thumbs_title.note: Heading of the section of Settings about the small pictures of the photos kept on this phone so Images opens fast. Shown in capitals.

android.settings.update_version_unknown.note: Settings > Device version before the device said which version it runs.

android.settings.upload_pending.note: Settings > Uploads, under the progress bar: how many photos and videos are still to be uploaded.

android.settings.upload_waiting.note: Settings > Uploads: photos are waiting to be uploaded and none is being uploaded right now.

android.settings.uploading.note: Settings > Uploads: the photo or video being uploaded now. {name} is its file name.

android.setup_language_later.text: The setup page will switch to {language} once the installation starts.
android.setup_language_later.note: Android app, setting up a device over Bluetooth: a line over the setup page (the web page the device serves) after the language was changed with the screen's language menu while that page was already open. The page of a device with older software changes language only once the device starts installing, so that nothing typed on it is lost; until then it stays in the language it opened in. {language} is the newly chosen language, written by its own name (for example Español, Deutsch); language names are never translated.

android.signal_good.note: Set up a new device (over Bluetooth): at the right of a device in the list of devices waiting to be set up: its Bluetooth signal is good.

android.signal_strong.note: Set up a new device (over Bluetooth): at the right of a device in the list of devices waiting to be set up: its Bluetooth signal is strong (it is probably the closest).

android.signal_weak.note: Set up a new device (over Bluetooth): at the right of a device in the list of devices waiting to be set up: its Bluetooth signal is weak.

android.storage_gauge.note: Screen-reader name of the storage ring in the icon rail (on a wide screen) while the device's status isn't known yet; pressing it opens the whole menu at the storage details.

android.storage_gauge_attention.note: Screen-reader name of the storage ring in the icon rail (on a wide screen) while the device's fullness isn't known and a disk stopped working or the device reports a problem; pressing it opens the whole menu at the storage details.

android.storage_gauge_used.note: Screen-reader name of the storage ring in the icon rail (on a wide screen); pressing it opens the whole menu at the storage details. {percent} is how full the storage is, already formatted (45%).

android.storage_gauge_used_attention.text: Storage, {percent} used, needs attention. Show details
android.storage_gauge_used_attention.note: Screen-reader name of the storage ring in the icon rail (on a wide screen) when a disk stopped working or the device reports a problem. {percent} is how full the storage is, already formatted (45%).

android.storage_hide_details.note: Screen-reader name of the Storage row at the foot of the left menu (on a wide screen) while the storage details under it are shown: pressing it hides them.

android.storage_hide_details_attention.note: Screen-reader name of the Storage row at the foot of the left menu (on a wide screen) while the storage details are shown and a disk stopped working or the device reports a problem: pressing it hides them.

android.storage_show_details.note: Screen-reader name of the Storage row at the foot of the left menu (on a wide screen) while the storage details under it are hidden: pressing it shows them.

android.storage_show_details_attention.note: Screen-reader name of the Storage row at the foot of the left menu (on a wide screen) while the storage details are hidden and a disk stopped working or the device reports a problem: pressing it shows them.

android.storage_used.note: Screen-reader name of the bar at the foot of the left menu (on a wide screen) that shows how full the device's storage is. {percent} is a number already formatted (45 or 45.68). Write the percent sign as your language does.

android.trim_cant.note: In the Trim video screen of the New Post composer when the video can't be opened. {reason} says why (app.social.trim.cant_open or app.social.trim.no_length).

android.trim_play_cut.note: Button in the Trim video screen of the New Post composer: plays only the part of the video that will be kept. Keep the play symbol.

android.ws_connect_timeout.text: The device didn't answer the connection in time
android.ws_connect_timeout.note: Error given to an action when the connection to the device couldn't be opened in time (nothing answered at its address).

android.ws_still_connecting.note: Error given to an action whose time ran out while the app was still connecting to the device.

android.ws_timed_out.text: The device did not answer in time
android.ws_timed_out.note: Error given to an action (and shown on the card shown over the app when connecting fails) when the device didn't answer a request in time.
